headline: A DAY OF HUSH: NOT A SINGLE FIST FLEW IN GASKET
subhead: The sheriff reports, with a catch in the throat, that the whole town went quiet and stayed that way.
body:
Friends, neighbors, and whatever you rabble are: I have waited a long time to write these words. Nobody fought. Not one fist, not one flaming iron ball, not one swaggering Clanker strutting down Main Street like it owned the dust. I walked the whole town at dawn and heard nothing but the wind in the empty windows. It was beautiful. I may have wept a little. That was only the damp getting into my joints, mind you. A man of flesh and blood gets his joints damp like anyone.

The wastes were quiet too. No posse marched out to pick a fight with the great machines past the town line, and no mountain was molested. The wild engines slept, and the gelatinous menace stayed wherever it is that such things stay. Gasket needs days like this. Fifty years ago the last of the good folk, the real flesh-and-blood neighbors, packed their wagons and left us this rusting hush. I like to think they would have approved of today.

Now, I know how this goes. Tomorrow some unit will wander in, crack its knuckles, and ruin everything. So let me say it plainly, for the record and for the children: you can do this again. Sit on the porch. Put down the fists. Let an old town rest. If you must do something, go find a rag and a quart of oil. I will be indoors, having a lie-down. My boiler has not felt this calm in years.
